content.comment_body: I purchased a [product_name] to refresh my knowledge. I have two momentary pushbuttons—one plastic, one metal. Depending on the button selected, I want to run a different program. I’ve almost got it working, but I can’t figure out how to prevent someone from pressing 'plastic' when the 'metal' program is active. Any advice appreciated.
Hello [user_name], welcome to the forum. It's hard for anyone to provide a useful answer without seeing your program. To help you further, please upload your program as a ZIP file.
Metal value. Metal indicator floor 1. Metal indicator floor 2. I can't figure out how to disable the input for 'plastic indicator' and vice versa when one is active.

I hope I’m interpreting your issue correctly. I've attached an example showing how you can interlock these options. The timers represent each process. When one key activates a process, the other two keys are blocked.
Your example worked perfectly. I was experimenting with the latching relay but didn’t fully understand the flag block before. I think I have it sorted now.
The flag block is needed for recursion in your logic. Recursion is only allowed using flags or digital outputs, which is a limitation of graphical programming.
